---
title: "repdist"
subtitle: "Comparing proteins and metaproteomes in protein representation space"
---

Identity-based measures compare proteins only by accession. Protein-level
Bray-Curtis, for example, treats two different accessions as unrelated even
when they share fold and function. Two metaproteomes can therefore hold
different accessions yet carry similar structural or functional protein
repertoires.

`repdist` uses protein representations (embeddings from a protein language
model; by default TM-Vec, whose cosine similarity is a predicted TM-score)
for two related tasks:

**A. Comparing samples.** Each sample is an abundance-weighted distribution of
its proteins in representation space. `sample_mmd()` compares two such
distributions by the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) under a Gaussian (RBF)
kernel, so different but closely related proteins partly match.

**B. Grouping proteins.** `protein_similarity()` turns pairwise similarities
into a weighted graph, keeping only pairs that pass a similarity threshold
and an alignment-coverage threshold. `bin_proteins()` partitions the graph by
Markov clustering (MCL), and `bin_glom()` sums protein counts within each
bin for count-based analyses such as DESeq2.

```
sequences ─ embed_proteins() / read_embeddings() ─► embeddings
                                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────┐
         ▼                                                             ▼
  sample_mmd(counts, x)                                 protein_similarity(x)
  samples × samples distance                            weighted protein graph
  (PERMANOVA, PCoA)                                              │
                                                          bin_proteins(S)  (MCL)
                                                                 │
                                                          bin_glom(counts, bins)
                                                          samples × bins counts
```

# Documentation

**[Reference](reference.html)**: what each function computes and how to call
it: embeddings, the MMD distance, the similarity graph and MCL bins, and
the QC plots.

**[Simulation](simulation.html)**: two benchmarks with known truth. A
controlled positive benchmark on CATH FunFam domains, where one group's
enriched proteins share a hidden family and no accession; and sequence-disjoint
contrasts between enzyme classes (EC3) of experimentally
characterised Swiss-Prot enzymes, against Bray-Curtis on MCL bins, MMseqs2
bins and proteins. Then how completely the MCL bins recover enzyme classes.

**[MCL parameters](parameters.html)**: how `min_sim`, `min_coverage` and
the MCL inflation change the bins, scored against the simulation's enzyme
labels.

**[Case study](case_study.html)**: a worked metaproteomics
analysis of a 20% yeast vs 20% casein diet comparison in mice: beta
diversity, the representation space, MCL bins and bin-level differential
abundance with DESeq2.

# Installation {#installation}

`repdist` is an R package (R >= 4.5). Install the development version from
GitHub:

```r
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Yixuan39/repdist")
```

`embed_proteins()` runs its models in a Python environment that `repdist`
creates and manages itself through `basilisk`; no manual Python setup is
needed. Model weights are downloaded on first use.

```r
library(repdist)
x <- embed_proteins("proteins.fasta")      # default model: "tmvec"

D <- sample_mmd(counts, x)                 # samples x samples dist
vegan::adonis2(D ~ group, data = metadata)

S <- protein_similarity(x)                 # weighted similarity graph
bins <- bin_proteins(S)                    # MCL bins
binned <- bin_glom(counts, bins)           # samples x bins counts
```

`counts` has samples in rows and proteins in columns, named as in `x`.
